title: Fresh off victory, Democrats gather with a warning: Don’t mess this up
description: Democrats at a convention in Denver tempered their big-win joy with concern that they could blow the opportunity.

title: With Miller in charge, hope fades for immigration compromise with Democrats
description: Trump and his DHS secretary say they are open to working with Democrats on immigration policy. Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff might change that.

title: Pentagon prepares its own prosecution of general accused of leaking
description: Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia now faces legal jeopardy on two fronts after allegations by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s team were previously referred to the Justice Department.

title: In calling for an end to the Iran War, Vance walks a thin line with Trump
description: A rift is opening up between President Trump and Vice President Vance when it comes to the Iran War. NPR's Ayesha Rascoe talks to Susan Glasser, staff writer at the New Yorker.

title: Politics chat: Duffy calls for more funding, Democrats plans for accountability
description: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy demands more money for the country's air travel control systems. Democrats plan for accountability, but not enough of them showed up for an impeachment vote.

title: Midterm voters ended the long-running GOP dominance in state legislatures
description: In several states, Democrats took control of legislatures that had been divided and they weakened GOP dominance in others. Issues on the agenda: More access to health care, new limits on school vouchers.

title: New Mexico wanted free childcare for all. This is what's worked — and what hasn't
description: A year ago in November, New Mexico became the first state to offer free childcare to every eligible family, regardless of income.

title: Judge temporarily blocks Trump from moving ahead on Washington public golf course redevelopment
description: A federal judge on Saturday ordered a two-week delay to any work at a historic Washington public golf course not far from the White House.

title: Majority of Americans disapprove of Trump’s construction projects, poll finds
description: The president’s efforts to remake Washington also face significant Republican opposition.

title: Chris Van Hollen revs up his public campaign to replace Chuck Schumer
description: The Democratic senator from Maryland launched a website and will hit the Sunday shows.

title: Florida city cancels St. Patrick's Day parade, citing new anti-DEI law
description: A new Florida law that prohibits taxpayer dollars from going toward diversity initiatives has prompted Delray Beach to cancel its St. Patrick's Day parade after a nearly 60-year run.

title: Judge in golf course case says inquiry into DOJ lawyers will proceed
description: The Trump administration’s attorneys have objected to a special master reviewing their conduct in the case.

title: 'We can't let them down' -- After midterm wins, Democrats turn to charting path ahead
description: Democrats from across the country descended on Denver for a two-day conference to chart the course of their party after sweeping victories in the midterm elections.

title: White evangelicals voted less, and less for the GOP, new analysis says
description: In 343 counties dubbed evangelical hubs, turnout was 66 percent of what it was in 2024, according to a new analysis.

title: Stephen Miller dresses like a reasonable man. But listen to what he says.
description: The new White House chief of staff understands how ordinary menswear can lend familiarity — and legitimacy — to an uncompromising worldview.

title: Nvidia scandal hits Trump’s political vulnerabilities after Democratic sweep
description: The scandal connects to voter concerns over AI, data centers, China and corruption.

title: Stephen Miller faces first crisis as White House chief of staff
description: Nvidia affair hit as the new chief of staff was deeply engaged in a reorganization of the White House staff and new policies toward Venezuela and trade.

title: A potential 2028 candidate takes himself out of the running, as others gear up
description: Your weekly guide to the biggest news in the 2028 presidential race.

title: Alaska voters aren't ditching ranked choice voting, top-four primaries
description: This is the second time Alaskans voted down an effort to repeal the state's unique election system, which voters first approved in 2020. A repeal effort in 2024 also failed narrowly.

title: Week in Politics: Battle for Senate leader; young and independent midterm turnout
description: The battle over the next majority leader in the U.S. Senate reflects the turnout by younger and independent voters in the midterm elections.

title: Legal scholar Stephen Vladeck on Texas' new Democratic AG and federal litigation
description: NPR's Scott Simon speaks with legal scholar and Georgetown professor Stephen Vladeck about Texas Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson, a Democrat, and what that could mean for federal litigation.

title: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins wins Alaska governor’s race
description: Kreiss-Tomkins, 37, defeated three Republicans, including President Donald Trump’s preferred candidate.

title: Few colleagues immediately embrace Van Hollen in his bid for majority leader
description: The Maryland Democrat said he believes there is a broad desire for change among Senate Democrats.

title: States can delay controversial Medicaid work requirement for six months
description: The postponement appeared to acknowledge states might need more time to smoothly implement the change.

title: Trump to have first trilateral meeting with Putin, Xi
description: President Donald Trump will meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping next week near the end of his Asia trip, the White House said Friday.

title: FBI arrests son of former CIA director John Brennan on child pornography charges
description: Kyle Brennan, 40, remained in federal custody Friday.

title: Brian Monahan out as attending physician to Congress amid Pentagon probe
description: An inspector general report this week also found that there had been insufficient oversight of Navy personnel assigned to his office.

title: Newly elected House Democrat under investigation for alleged sexual harassment
description: Rep.-elect Brian Poindexter, who defeated embattled incumbent Max Miller in Ohio, was accused by a former campaign volunteer.

title: Supreme Court to review Trump policy blocking asylum seekers at border
description: The case is the latest immigration issue the justices will weigh in the coming months.

title: Van Hollen ‘no longer pursuing’ possible 2028 bid as he seeks Senate leader job
description: Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D) said Friday he has abandoned a potential bid for the presidency and will seek to lead the Senate instead.

title: Rep. Lauren Boebert ousted in Colorado’s conservative 4th District
description: Democrat Eileen Laubacher unseated Boebert, a MAGA acolyte with a slate of controversies in her personal life that have spilled into public view.

title: Biden defends his 2024 run and reckons with Trump in his new memoir
description: In “Promise Me, America,” the former president revisits the pandemic and the conflict in Gaza, and explains his decision to seek a second term.

title: Stacey Abrams told Ava DuVernay to hold ‘14th’ until after midterms
description: The “Selma” filmmaker’s latest documentary traces the history of the 14th Amendment.

title: Trump gives Scott Colom ‘a lot of credit’ for campaigning at a MAGA rally
description: Scott Colom made reaching out to Trump supporters central to his U.S. Senate campaign in Mississippi.

description: The movement’s rank and file, young and old, are soul-searching as they look to leaders outside the White House, cross over to Democrats or disengage from politics.

title: Trump’s Cabinet secretaries get some bad press
description: What happened this week under the Trump administration.

title: Trump falsely claims ‘nobody’s been killed’ in Iran war ‘in the last five months’
description: In July, three soldiers died in an enemy attack on an air base in Jordan, another died at an air base in Iraq and a Navy captain died during an emergency landing in the Arabian Sea.
